2.scope: Finite-field tests for arbitrary nonzero outer row/column scalings and permutations of a normalized dyadic DFT. Two-column/cross-ratio tests are one-sided; full_monomial_gate is a complete test only for an explicitly materialized square matrix in its supported field domain.
2.math: Anchoring Aij*A00/(Ai0*A0j) removes row/column gauges. A primitive odd exponent for power-of-two N fixes a separable exponent grid; complete alpha/beta residue permutations plus all-entry equality reconstruct a genuine outer gauge. The root helper partial read confirms N>=2, power-of-two and N|(P-1). Histogram tests correctly remain necessary rather than sufficient.
2.guards: Square/full gate uses an assert; primitive-root support is delegated. Oracle length/type/linearity/determinism and canonical residues are assumed. cross_ratio_witness tests 0 literally rather than modulo P; short outputs index-fail. MaskedPermutedFFT assumes x has exactly N elements.

Dense oracle extraction needs N oracle calls and Theta(N^2) storage. 6.scope: v10 arbitrary-length approximate normalized DFT lift through Q=next-power-of-two(N), using nearest-grid residual Taylor or Jacobi-Anger/Chebyshev expansion and a randomized dyadic chirp row, then majority-grid aggregation.
6.math: The decomposition uses scale sqrt(Q/N), grid phases and residual theta in [-1/2,1/2]; Taylor/Bessel tails control each output error by tail*||x||2 through Cauchy-Schwarz. Reusing the same chirp state across terms is the intended fixed-output linearity/variance mechanism. The statistical radius is a coordinatewise uniform-over-outputs bound for a fixed input and random rows, conditional on the core theorem; it is not a spectral operator norm or exact all-input transform. fixed_row_g algebraically inverts 2N*comb(rows,s)*g^(-2s).
6.guards: Positive n and dyadic Q helpers exist, tolerance/rows/delta guards exist, but rank, g, shape and finiteness are inconsistent. Rank-zero direct-vs-lift discrepancy and N=1 streaming rejection are concrete. float nearest-grid arithmetic is unsuitable as exact arbitrary-large integer rounding; uniqueness catches collisions but cannot certify exact offsets at huge sizes. Tiny tolerance rank searches can encounter overflow/underflow outside tested ranges.
6.cost: Approximate rows perform rank core transforms plus rank*N combination, storing rank coefficient arrays. Per-row O(rank*N) coefficient memory and repeated mapping/Bessel setup are material. Control paths call np.fft.fft or explicit O(rank*N^2) kernels. run_experiments retains 1,200 sampled vectors for variance; this experiment is not streaming-memory verification. Formal large-N work_proxy values are not benchmarks.
6.tests: The separate test suite exercises positive ranks and modest sizes, exhaustive small random-state floating enumeration and one seeded robust test. main prints PASS regardless of metrics. No supplied code or tests were executed.

20.scope: Exact modular parity-block Harper/Fourier polynomial reconstruction and distinct zero-mode Fourier eigenphase certificates for dyadic N.
20.math: Sparse reflection bases yield even dimension N/2+1 and odd N/2-1. A nonzero-offdiagonal Jacobi Krylov first-row basis gives a triangular solve for p(H); the source then verifies each full matrix column by Horner application. Nonzero top coefficient establishes each finite degree. Both blocks have a zero H eigenvector but different F phases, obstructing one scalar function of H on the full space. These are meaningful complete finite checks, not fast transforms.
20.guards: root_n assert enforces 4<=N<=2^23 dyadic; square-root p prime is assumed. Parity sign treats all non-1 values as odd. Component dictionaries are trusted. Expected odd coefficient uses an unbounded integer power before modular reduction.

23.scope: Phase18 primitive-Weyl necessary gate for fixed invertible outer Green-sum matrices and a middle diagonal or monomial.
23.math: For M=AQB, MZ=DM implies UQ=QV with U=A^-1DA,V=BZB^-1. Diagonal and pair-product multisets are invariant under monomial conjugacy, so mismatch soundly excludes all middle monomials for those fixed stages. Matching invariants are only necessary. Graph ratio propagation exactly solves a nonzero diagonal for a fixed indexing, but one primitive identity alone admits diagonal-after-Fourier freedom and does not certify F.

24.scope: Operator-norm lower bound from a separated Fourier submatrix for q-path Green sums and finite numerical checks on sampled order families.
24.math: Uses m=floor(N/2^q), W=q*half_bandwidth and the valid nontrivial-regime bound sqrt((m^2/N-W)/(m-W)); otherwise returns zero. For a separated m-by-m submatrix with ||F_sub||<=1 and Frobenius square m^2/N, the (W+1)st singular value is at least the expression. The imported separator must actually deliver disjoint equally sized row/column sets separated in every order; this file does not independently verify that contract.
24.guards: No n/q/bandwidth integer/positivity validation; instance_gap assumes q>=1 and uses W=q only. It enforces m>W and m^2>WN via assertions, then indexes singular[W]. Negative q/bandwidth or malformed separator outputs are not supported explicitly.
